summary.oneLiner: A modest quarter — INR316cr revenue at ~7% YoY with 11.1% EBITDA margin — where the operating problem is not demand but conversion: customers are signing contracts and then deferring start dates because *their own* cash flows are stressed by the restarted conflict. Management explicitly refused to give numeric guidance, committing only to "meet or beat" last year's growth rate, backed by a nine-month order book. The genuine change this quarter is the IP shift: Phoenix.ai won a 4-million-lines-of-code modernization mandate, Structi.ai launched, and a new Action Energy JV targets 5% of a USD1bn GCC digital-oilfield market over three years.

> Adjustments / one-offs: none flagged. Kumori (the ServiceNow acquisition) contributed only ~INR4cr of quarterly revenue — management was explicit it was bought "for capability and not revenue," so it is not a growth driver.
guidance (critical — verify next quarter:
- **Revenue growth:** **no numeric guidance given**, and management explained why — "whatever guidance I might give may not be [reliable]… because of what is happening to the global environment." The only committed statement: **FY27 growth will "meet or beat" the growth rate achieved in FY26.** Also declined 2–3 year guidance entirely, noting even large IT companies are now giving only one-year guidance.
- **Margin:** none given.
- **Order book / inflow target:** **nine months of order-book visibility** confirmed as the basis for the growth statement.
- **Capex / commissioning dates:** none. Capital-markets item: the **second tranche of the ~USD50mn FCCB programme is delayed** but management insisted "It is going to happen. It's just a matter of time."
- **JV target (dated):** **Action Energy JV to capture 5% of the ~USD1bn GCC digital-oilfield transformation market within three years**; entry via **Kuwait first**, then other GCC countries.
order book & pipeline:
The only quantified visibility metric is duration: "We have order books for nine months. So, there is a predictable revenue for the next nine months." The stated constraint on converting pipeline to revenue is **delayed starts** — customers complete negotiations, then push contract execution out by a month at a time because they are worried about their own cash flow. Management framed this as demand deferred rather than demand lost: "there is demand out there. It's just people are not… getting us to let us start."

New client wins in the quarter (all unnamed, described by profile):
1. A Fortune India 500 conglomerate — unified enterprise workflow platform on Kellton's low-code/no-code stack, modernising financial and governance processes, leading to AI-assisted process automation.
2. A leading UAE enterprise group — cloud-native "enterprise operating system" unifying operations, governance, finance and workflows with API-led integration and AI-driven insights.
3. A Middle East energy infrastructure company — enterprise workflow platform digitising time-critical, regulatory-approval-bearing operational processes.
4. A global industrial services enterprise (recently closed a large funding round) — engineering on a mission-critical field-operations platform.
5. A global pest-management leader — cloud-native intelligent field-service and customer-engagement platform on GCP with AI-assisted scheduling, technician route optimisation and ERP/middleware integration.
segment / subsidiary detail:
- **Optima (digital oil fields)** — the Oil India deployment was completed in **under six months** across **46 sites and ~80 wells** in difficult Northeast terrain, sensors through to platform. This is the reference asset behind the GCC JV.
- **Phoenix.ai** — legacy-modernization accelerator claiming **~80% faster at half the cost**. Won an enterprise modernization mandate covering **4 million lines of code** on a specialised ERP, on aggressive timelines. A customer-acquisition campaign has been launched to find similar legacy estates.
- **Structi.ai** — newly launched AI context engine converting unstructured enterprise data into AI-ready intelligence (metadata enrichment, intelligent data orchestration, generative AI). Positioned as the prerequisite layer: "before you can do any AI, you really need to have your data in order." *Note: `companies.csv` records this product as "Structy.ai"; the transcript consistently says **Structi.ai**.*
- **KAI (internal)** — delivery-efficiency platform delivering **~30% efficiency gains** in testing, business development and business-analysis work.
- **Kumori / ServiceNow** — bought for certifications and case studies, not revenue (~INR4cr/quarter). The stated problem it solved: customers checking the ServiceNow partner portal saw no activity or case studies for Kellton. Those case studies are now Kellton's, and management attributes client wins to it.
- **Snowflake** — moved up to **Select Tier partner** this quarter.
- **Government** — BW Businessworld People Tech Future Awards 2026 gold award for the Government of Karnataka HRMS2 programme covering **55 departments and 5 lakh+ employees**. Also flagged as a slow-paying customer class.
- **Other delivery** — modernized an enterprise platform for a global agriculture company; modernized loan origination and sales portal for an NBFC, enabling a new loan-against-property offering.
growth verticals / optionality:
- **Action Energy JV (GCC)** — the clearest new optionality. Management was candid that "that GCC market is unknown to us" beyond a small UAE presence, so it bought local knowledge, relationships and delivery capability via partnership rather than building. Scope extends beyond digital oilfields into AI-led transformation for other regional companies. Explicitly no pipeline built yet: "At this point, I don't have a pipeline built."
- **AI as embedded content, not a separate line** — "there is a component of AI in every project that we are doing now, unlike before." Pure-AI projects are acknowledged to be small; the value is AI attach-rate on transformation work.
- **Partnership-led growth** — deliberate investment into ServiceNow, Microsoft and Snowflake as demand channels.
- **Installed-base re-engagement** — reaching back to previously serviced customers with newly acquired platform and product offerings.
6a. moat & competitive position:
- **Proprietary accelerators with quantified economics.** Phoenix.ai is claimed at 80% faster / ~50% of competitor pricing, evidenced by the 4-million-line win. KAI delivers ~30% internal efficiency in specific functions. These are the only defensible assets a company of this size has against larger IT firms.
- **Positioning against "AI as an add-on."** Management drew the distinction sharply: "most of the companies that we are seeing are just slapping on AI as an add-on. For us, AI is not that. We take it to the core." Unverified, but it is the stated differentiation.
- **Anti-moat, stated candidly:** no pricing power on payment terms. "We are a small company. We are not like the large companies that have the muscle power to negotiate. For us, it's like, take it or leave it."
margins & cost dynamics: EBITDA margin of 11.1% and PAT margin of 7.1% were reported without a cost bridge; no margin commentary or guidance was offered on the call. The implicit margin lever discussed was KAI-driven delivery efficiency (~30% in testing/BD/BA). The working-capital drag is structural rather than cyclical: Fortune 100 US clients where "our clock begins after 90 days," plus Indian government, LIC and HRMS customers with long invoice-clearing cycles, produce **100+ days DSO**. Management stressed receivables are collected, not provisioned — write-offs are "a handful of crores over a period of one year or so" against disputes.
capex / expansion (watch slippage):
No physical capex. Expansion is via partnership and IP:
- **Action Energy JV** — Kuwait entry first, other GCC to follow; no dated milestones beyond the three-year 5%-market-share ambition.
- **FCCB tranche 2** — of the ~USD50mn programme, round 1 is done; round 2 is deferred on "global headwinds" and IT sector sentiment. Management is "waiting and watching."
capital allocation: Two visible uses: the Kumori acquisition (capability purchase, deliberately not revenue-accretive) and IP build-out (Phoenix.ai, Structi.ai, KAI). Funding is the FCCB programme, half-executed. No dividend, buyback or leverage commentary. The receivables position means a material share of reported profit is tied up in working capital — a call-out worth tracking against the FCCB delay, since a deferred capital raise plus 100+ day DSO is a liquidity combination that constrains growth investment.
risks & watch-items:
- **Delayed starts.** The core near-term risk, and the reason guidance was withheld — signed contracts not converting to billable work because customers are protecting their own cash.
- **Geopolitics.** "We thought that the war is going to end and it has restarted." Directly affecting US customer behaviour and the FCCB timing.
- **Receivables concentration and duration.** 100+ days DSO with a stated inability to negotiate better terms; absolute receivables grow with revenue by construction.
- **AI as a threat, acknowledged.** Management named "the AI impact that is out there" as a reason multi-year guidance is impossible — an honest admission that the services model itself may be repriced.
- **Structurally low disclosure.** No segment revenue, no geography split, no headcount, no client concentration, no order-book value, no margin bridge. All client wins are anonymised. This limits any independent verification of the growth story.
- **JV with no pipeline.** The Action Energy 5%/three-year target was set before any pipeline exists, by management's own admission.
- **FCCB tranche 2 slippage** — an unfunded balance sheet plan.
management quality / tone: Refreshingly unwilling to fabricate guidance — Niranjan Chintam repeatedly declined to give quarterly, annual or three-year numbers and explained the reasoning rather than deflecting. He answered the receivables question directly and unflatteringly ("that's not a reflection of our inability. It's just that we don't have the muscle power to negotiate"), conceded Kumori was bought for capability rather than revenue, and admitted the GCC JV has no pipeline yet. Against that, the call was thin on financial substance: no segment or geography detail, all client names withheld, and the one commitment made ("meet or beat last year") is anchored to an undisclosed base. The Q&A was almost entirely individual investors, with no institutional analysts — worth noting as a coverage signal.
non-obvious takeaways:
- The commitment is deliberately slippery: "meet or beat what we grew last year" is a promise about the *growth rate*, not the revenue level, and the FY26 base rate was not stated on the call. Verification next quarter requires pulling FY26 growth independently.
- Kumori is a case study in buying credibility rather than revenue — the acquisition thesis was literally that the ServiceNow partner portal showed no case studies. At ~INR4cr/quarter it will never justify itself on P&L, only on win-rate.
- The delayed-starts phenomenon is a *leading* indicator: revenue is already contracted, so a resolution of customer cash-flow stress would convert quickly. That makes the nine-month order book more meaningful than the 7% growth print.
- Phoenix.ai's pricing claim (half of what competitors charge) is a deliberate margin trade — it wins share in legacy modernization but caps realisation. Watch whether EBITDA margin holds at ~11% as Phoenix.ai-led work scales.
- The product name in our store is stale: transcript says **Structi.ai**, `companies.csv` says "Structy.ai."

themes.title: AI-led IT services & ER&D transformation
themes.need: Q1FY27 split the bucket three ways: a soft large-cap core, a re-accelerating mid-cap tier, and an outright business-model change. TCS grew constant currency only +0.4% QoQ / +3.2% YoY despite $9.5bn of TCV (including an ~$800mn net-new SKF mega-deal), and its AI-services book annualising $2.6bn (+13.6% QoQ) saw incremental adds DECELERATE from +$125mn to +$75mn - AI is still project revenue, not annuity. WIPRO is the laggard (+0.9% YoY cc, margin -120bps to 16.0%, Q2 guided -1.5% to +0.5%). Mid-caps are outgrowing: TECHM grew +6.6% YoY cc with every vertical up and an 11th consecutive quarter of margin expansion (14.4%, +330bps); MPHASIS's pipeline is at an all-time high, 2.8x its size at the Mphasis.ai launch and +28% YoY, with AI-led deals now 70% of it (from 12%) and BFS pipeline +100% YoY, and its new Tria platform closed multiple opportunities within seven weeks of launch; FRACTAL lifted net income +92% YoY on INR 912.5cr revenue at NRR 117% with zero churn (though only +9% cc, dragged by TMT -22%); KPITTECH won $349M of new deals with 21% of pipeline now productized AI/SDV solutions. Structurally, HCLTECH is entering the AI-datacenter business with an initial investment of up to INR 3,500cr and a 50MW long-term ambition, and PERSISTENT is buying Nagarro at EUR 1.27bn EV to build a $2.9bn / 46,000-person group - European scale is now bought, not built. The new cost line is visas: TATAELXSI crossed INR 1,000cr of quarterly revenue for the first time (INR 1,021.1cr) yet EBIT fell 330bps QoQ, with 220-230bps of it onsite/subcontractor investment the CFO said cannot be passed to customers.
themes.driver: MPHASIS's guide that 'Q2 is positioned to deliver the best sequential constant currency growth we have delivered in three years' is the most falsifiable claim in the sector; then HCLTECH's AI-datacenter build, the PERSISTENT-Nagarro close, and whether TCS's AI incremental adds re-accelerate off +$75mn.

hero.oneLiner: A modest quarter — INR316cr revenue at ~7% YoY with 11.1% EBITDA margin — where the operating problem is not demand but conversion: customers are signing contracts and then deferring start dates because *their own* cash flows are stressed by the restarted conflict. Management explicitly refused to give numeric guidance, committing only to "meet or beat" last year's growth rate, backed by a nine-month order book. The genuine change this quarter is the IP shift: Phoenix.ai won a 4-million-lines-of-code modernization mandate, Structi.ai launched, and a new Action Energy JV targets 5% of a USD1bn GCC digital-oilfield market over three years.

business_model.title: Positioning (investor deck)
business_model.body:
- Described as founded 2009 with "15+ years of experience", a footprint across "US, APAC, Middle East, Europe", and core strength stated as "ISO: 9001-015 CMMi Level 5".
- Scale credentials cited: 2000+ Projects Delivered, 500+ Clients Served, 50+ Fortune 500 Clients, 15+ Industries Catered To and 10+ Centres of Excellence.
- Deck's business split is shown as Digital Transformation (83.9%), Enterprise Solutions (13.3%) and Other Services (2.8%) — the deck gives the percentages without labelling the denominator.
- Strategy is framed around an "AI - First Delivery Engine" with "AI embedded across design, build, deploy, run", supported by ecosystem and hyperscaler partnerships, AI-ready talent & IP, client-led innovation, and governance & security.
- Named user industries: Banking, Financial Services & Institutions; Healthcare & Life science; Information Services & Technology; Retail and Business Services.

segment_detail.title: Segment / subsidiary detail
segment_detail.body:
- **Optima (digital oil fields)** — the Oil India deployment was completed in **under six months** across **46 sites and ~80 wells** in difficult Northeast terrain, sensors through to platform. This is the reference asset behind the GCC JV.
- **Phoenix.ai** — legacy-modernization accelerator claiming **~80% faster at half the cost**. Won an enterprise modernization mandate covering **4 million lines of code** on a specialised ERP, on aggressive timelines. A customer-acquisition campaign has been launched to find similar legacy estates.
- **Structi.ai** — newly launched AI context engine converting unstructured enterprise data into AI-ready intelligence (metadata enrichment, intelligent data orchestration, generative AI). Positioned as the prerequisite layer: "before you can do any AI, you really need to have your data in order." *Note: `companies.csv` records this product as "Structy.ai"; the transcript consistently says **Structi.ai**.*
- **KAI (internal)** — delivery-efficiency platform delivering **~30% efficiency gains** in testing, business development and business-analysis work.
- **Kumori / ServiceNow** — bought for certifications and case studies, not revenue (~INR4cr/quarter). The stated problem it solved: customers checking the ServiceNow partner portal saw no activity or case studies for Kellton. Those case studies are now Kellton's, and management attributes client wins to it.
- **Snowflake** — moved up to **Select Tier partner** this quarter.
- **Government** — BW Businessworld People Tech Future Awards 2026 gold award for the Government of Karnataka HRMS2 programme covering **55 departments and 5 lakh+ employees**. Also flagged as a slow-paying customer class.
- **Other delivery** — modernized an enterprise platform for a global agriculture company; modernized loan origination and sales portal for an NBFC, enabling a new loan-against-property offering.

order_book.title: Order book & pipeline
order_book.body:
The only quantified visibility metric is duration: "We have order books for nine months. So, there is a predictable revenue for the next nine months." The stated constraint on converting pipeline to revenue is **delayed starts** — customers complete negotiations, then push contract execution out by a month at a time because they are worried about their own cash flow. Management framed this as demand deferred rather than demand lost: "there is demand out there. It's just people are not… getting us to let us start."

New client wins in the quarter (all unnamed, described by profile):
1. A Fortune India 500 conglomerate — unified enterprise workflow platform on Kellton's low-code/no-code stack, modernising financial and governance processes, leading to AI-assisted process automation.
2. A leading UAE enterprise group — cloud-native "enterprise operating system" unifying operations, governance, finance and workflows with API-led integration and AI-driven insights.
3. A Middle East energy infrastructure company — enterprise workflow platform digitising time-critical, regulatory-approval-bearing operational processes.
4. A global industrial services enterprise (recently closed a large funding round) — engineering on a mission-critical field-operations platform.
5. A global pest-management leader — cloud-native intelligent field-service and customer-engagement platform on GCP with AI-assisted scheduling, technician route optimisation and ERP/middleware integration.

guidance.title: Guidance (CRITICAL — verify next quarter)
guidance.body:
- **Revenue growth:** **no numeric guidance given**, and management explained why — "whatever guidance I might give may not be [reliable]… because of what is happening to the global environment." The only committed statement: **FY27 growth will "meet or beat" the growth rate achieved in FY26.** Also declined 2–3 year guidance entirely, noting even large IT companies are now giving only one-year guidance.
- **Margin:** none given.
- **Order book / inflow target:** **nine months of order-book visibility** confirmed as the basis for the growth statement.
- **Capex / commissioning dates:** none. Capital-markets item: the **second tranche of the ~USD50mn FCCB programme is delayed** but management insisted "It is going to happen. It's just a matter of time."
- **JV target (dated):** **Action Energy JV to capture 5% of the ~USD1bn GCC digital-oilfield transformation market within three years**; entry via **Kuwait first**, then other GCC countries.

growth_optionality.title: Growth verticals / optionality
growth_optionality.body:
- **Action Energy JV (GCC)** — the clearest new optionality. Management was candid that "that GCC market is unknown to us" beyond a small UAE presence, so it bought local knowledge, relationships and delivery capability via partnership rather than building. Scope extends beyond digital oilfields into AI-led transformation for other regional companies. Explicitly no pipeline built yet: "At this point, I don't have a pipeline built."
- **AI as embedded content, not a separate line** — "there is a component of AI in every project that we are doing now, unlike before." Pure-AI projects are acknowledged to be small; the value is AI attach-rate on transformation work.
- **Partnership-led growth** — deliberate investment into ServiceNow, Microsoft and Snowflake as demand channels.
- **Installed-base re-engagement** — reaching back to previously serviced customers with newly acquired platform and product offerings.

margins.title: Margins & cost dynamics
margins.body: EBITDA margin of 11.1% and PAT margin of 7.1% were reported without a cost bridge; no margin commentary or guidance was offered on the call. The implicit margin lever discussed was KAI-driven delivery efficiency (~30% in testing/BD/BA). The working-capital drag is structural rather than cyclical: Fortune 100 US clients where "our clock begins after 90 days," plus Indian government, LIC and HRMS customers with long invoice-clearing cycles, produce **100+ days DSO**. Management stressed receivables are collected, not provisioned — write-offs are "a handful of crores over a period of one year or so" against disputes.

capital_allocation.title: Capital allocation
capital_allocation.body: Two visible uses: the Kumori acquisition (capability purchase, deliberately not revenue-accretive) and IP build-out (Phoenix.ai, Structi.ai, KAI). Funding is the FCCB programme, half-executed. No dividend, buyback or leverage commentary. The receivables position means a material share of reported profit is tied up in working capital — a call-out worth tracking against the FCCB delay, since a deferred capital raise plus 100+ day DSO is a liquidity combination that constrains growth investment.

management_tone.title: Management quality / tone
management_tone.body: Refreshingly unwilling to fabricate guidance — Niranjan Chintam repeatedly declined to give quarterly, annual or three-year numbers and explained the reasoning rather than deflecting. He answered the receivables question directly and unflatteringly ("that's not a reflection of our inability. It's just that we don't have the muscle power to negotiate"), conceded Kumori was bought for capability rather than revenue, and admitted the GCC JV has no pipeline yet. Against that, the call was thin on financial substance: no segment or geography detail, all client names withheld, and the one commitment made ("meet or beat last year") is anchored to an undisclosed base. The Q&A was almost entirely individual investors, with no institutional analysts — worth noting as a coverage signal.

moat.title: 6a. Moat & competitive position
moat.body:
- **Proprietary accelerators with quantified economics.** Phoenix.ai is claimed at 80% faster / ~50% of competitor pricing, evidenced by the 4-million-line win. KAI delivers ~30% internal efficiency in specific functions. These are the only defensible assets a company of this size has against larger IT firms.
- **Positioning against "AI as an add-on."** Management drew the distinction sharply: "most of the companies that we are seeing are just slapping on AI as an add-on. For us, AI is not that. We take it to the core." Unverified, but it is the stated differentiation.
- **Anti-moat, stated candidly:** no pricing power on payment terms. "We are a small company. We are not like the large companies that have the muscle power to negotiate. For us, it's like, take it or leave it."

risks.title: Risks & watch-items
risks.body:
- **Delayed starts.** The core near-term risk, and the reason guidance was withheld — signed contracts not converting to billable work because customers are protecting their own cash.
- **Geopolitics.** "We thought that the war is going to end and it has restarted." Directly affecting US customer behaviour and the FCCB timing.
- **Receivables concentration and duration.** 100+ days DSO with a stated inability to negotiate better terms; absolute receivables grow with revenue by construction.
- **AI as a threat, acknowledged.** Management named "the AI impact that is out there" as a reason multi-year guidance is impossible — an honest admission that the services model itself may be repriced.
- **Structurally low disclosure.** No segment revenue, no geography split, no headcount, no client concentration, no order-book value, no margin bridge. All client wins are anonymised. This limits any independent verification of the growth story.
- **JV with no pipeline.** The Action Energy 5%/three-year target was set before any pipeline exists, by management's own admission.
- **FCCB tranche 2 slippage** — an unfunded balance sheet plan.

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious takeaways
non_obvious.body:
- The commitment is deliberately slippery: "meet or beat what we grew last year" is a promise about the *growth rate*, not the revenue level, and the FY26 base rate was not stated on the call. Verification next quarter requires pulling FY26 growth independently.
- Kumori is a case study in buying credibility rather than revenue — the acquisition thesis was literally that the ServiceNow partner portal showed no case studies. At ~INR4cr/quarter it will never justify itself on P&L, only on win-rate.
- The delayed-starts phenomenon is a *leading* indicator: revenue is already contracted, so a resolution of customer cash-flow stress would convert quickly. That makes the nine-month order book more meaningful than the 7% growth print.
- Phoenix.ai's pricing claim (half of what competitors charge) is a deliberate margin trade — it wins share in legacy modernization but caps realisation. Watch whether EBITDA margin holds at ~11% as Phoenix.ai-led work scales.
- The product name in our store is stale: transcript says **Structi.ai**, `companies.csv` says "Structy.ai."

qoq_log.body:

Five new logo wins (Fortune India 500 conglomerate, UAE enterprise group, Middle East energy infrastructure, global industrial services, global pest management). Oil India Optima digital-oilfield deployment completed in under six months across 46 sites / ~80 wells. **Phoenix.ai won a 4-million-lines-of-code modernization mandate; Structi.ai launched; Snowflake Select Tier partnership achieved; new Action Energy JV for GCC (Kuwait first) targeting 5% of a USD1bn market in three years.** Gold award for Karnataka HRMS2. Kumori contributing only ~INR4cr/quarter (capability buy). FCCB tranche 2 delayed. DSO 100+ days. **No numeric guidance given — only "meet or beat" FY26 growth.**

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
